---
title: "Use flashier.utils with AI assistants"
description: "Install the flashier.utils agent skill in Claude Code or another coding agent, or point any assistant at llms.txt."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

flashier.utils offers two things for AI coding assistants. The first is an
agent skill: instructions that teach an assistant the package's workflow, its
required declarations and its traps. The second is an `llms.txt` file that any
assistant able to read a web page can use.

## Claude Code

Run these two commands inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add mdmanurung/flashier-utils
/plugin install flashier-utils@flashier-utils
```

The skill then loads on its own when you ask about flashier fits, factor
interpretation, association tests, projection or consensus references.

The assistant runs R code in your environment, so install the package there too:

```r
remotes::install_github("mdmanurung/flashier-utils")
```

## Other coding agents

The skill follows the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format, so
any agent that reads skills can use it. Copy the skill directory into your
agent's skills folder:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mdmanurung/flashier-utils
cp -r flashier-utils/skills/flashier-utils <your-agent-skills-dir>/
```

Common locations are `.agents/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/` and
`~/.codex/skills/`; check your agent's documentation.

## Any assistant: llms.txt

Give the assistant this URL, or paste the file's contents into the chat:

<https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/llms.txt>

The file is generated from this website at every build. It lists the
tutorials and the function reference in plain Markdown.

## What the skill contains

- `SKILL.md` holds the core workflow (fit, view, features, plots), the
  declarations the package will not guess (`sample_side`, `feature_scale`,
  `unit_col`, `seed`) and the common traps. Examples of traps are sign
  ambiguity, opposite contrast directions and treating cells as replicates.
- `references/inference.md` covers group summaries, association tests,
  back-projection, posterior uncertainty, stability and held-out prediction.
- `references/projection-and-references.md` covers projection onto new samples
  and the experimental consensus references across datasets.
- `references/fitting.md` covers prior families, batch correction, GBCD,
  grade-of-membership DE and membership filtering.

Every code snippet in the skill was run against the package before release.
The skill does not replace the function reference. An assistant can still make
mistakes, so check its code and its scientific claims as you would a
colleague's.

The skill format and this page follow the example of
[Marsilea](https://marsilea.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ai_assistants.html)
(the Marsilea-viz project); no Marsilea text or code is reused.
